Run the cascade over a large grant file in checkpointed batches

Source: R/batch.R
pf_run_batches.Rd

Run the cascade over a large grant file in checkpointed batches

Usage

pf_run_batches(
  grants,
  ref,
  dir = "data-dev/batches",
  batch_size = 25000L,
  passes = c(pf_staged_passes("lean"), pf_recovery_passes(state = TRUE)),
  config = npmatch::np_config(),
  method = "hier",
  recover = TRUE,
  self_guard = TRUE,
  dyads = NULL,
  dyad_config = pf_dyad_config(),
  resume = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  check_reference = c("auto", "stop", "warn", "ignore")
)

Arguments

grants

A prepared frame from pf_prepare_grants(), ideally already deduplicated by pf_dedup() and reduced with pf_recipients().

ref

A reference bundle from pf_build_reference().

dir

Checkpoint directory. Created if absent.

batch_size

Identities per batch. Smaller batches checkpoint more often and lose less on an interrupt; larger ones amortise per-batch overhead.

passes, config, method, recover

Passed to pf_match_grants().

self_guard

Apply pf_drop_self_matches() to each batch.

dyads

Optional dyad table from pf_build_dyads(). When given, pf_dyad_collapse() runs on each batch before the status frame is built, and the status gains dyad_collapsed, dyad_id, dyad_class, dyad_alt_ein and dyad_from_ein. See Where the collapse runs.

dyad_config

Settings for that collapse; see pf_dyad_config().

resume

Reuse batches whose checkpoint file already exists and whose run stamp matches this call. A checkpoint written under different settings is an error, not a cache hit; see Checkpoints are stamped.

verbose

Per-batch progress.

Value

A data frame: the concatenated per-identity pf_status() frames, with a batch column. Timings are attached as attr(, "timing").

Where the collapse runs

Between pf_drop_self_matches() and pf_status(), because that is the only point at which the scored pairs still exist — the status frame keeps just the winning candidate. Collapsing is resolved within one grant's candidate list only, so a per-batch collapse is identical to a whole-file one; batching cannot change the answer.

Checkpoints are stamped

Every checkpoint carries a pf_stamp attribute recording what produced it: reference size and column set, the normalizer signature, the pass table, the npmatch::np_config(), method, recover, self_guard, and the shape of dyads with its dyad_config. On resume the stamp must match this call or pf_run_batches() stops.

This guards a specific silent failure, measured in dev/REFIT-1K-FINDINGS.md §3a: calling pf_link() twice on one directory, first with policy = "query" and then with policy = "operating", returned identical EINs both times — every batch came off disk and the changed config was never applied. Nothing in the output distinguishes that from a real run. A wasted recomputation costs hours; an unnoticed stale one costs the result.

Checkpoints written before stamping existed carry no stamp and cannot be verified, so they are refused for the same reason. To recompute and overwrite, pass resume = FALSE; to start clean, delete dir.
